newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela official sees 1997 growth of 4 percent.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela official sees 1997 growth of 4 percent.

text.p: Venezuela's economy could grow four percent this year as the government's economic program begins to bear fruit, a senior government official said.
Trade and Industry Minister Freddy Rojas Parra told the foreign press association the economy grew one percent in the first quarter of the year, and around 1.5 percent over the first half.

"Our forecasts see a real bounce in economic growth for the second half of the year," he said, adding however that Planning Ministry forecasts of over five percent growth for 1997 were more likely to be realized from 1988 onwards.

Rojas said signs of a robust pick-up in Venezuelan demand included a 1.24 percent increase in electricity consumption over the first four months of the year, a 41.8 percent increase in cement and steel rod sales over the same period, a 20 percent first quarter rise in chemical sales, and a surging 166 percent first half increase in vehicle sales.

Economic growth, led by construction in the east of the country, one of the main sites of Venezuela's recent oil opening, would reduce unemployment by about two percentage points by year-end from current levels of 12.6 percent, he said.

Rojas added that a 24.7 percent increase in bank lending between January and May was a further sign Venezuela was finally emerging from a recession which saw the economy shrink 1.5 percent in 1996 and inflation reach triple digits.
Rojas reiterated inflation targets of between 30 and 32 percent for this year.
